rows.label: Pot holders on the shelf

rows.ask: Plenty of stock, so you're safe?
rows.ask_tts: [short pause] Plenty of stock, so you're safe?
rows.why: Units sold in the last 30 days, divided by 30.

rows.label: Days to sell out (130 / 0.9)
rows.say: Nope. That's 144 days to sell out.
rows.tts: Nope. That's a hundred forty-four days to sell out.
rows.why: Days of stock = units on hand / units sold per day: 130 / 0.9 = 144.4.

rows.label: Cash tied up (130 x $5.10 cost)
rows.say: At $5.10 cost each, that's $663 of cash. Sitting there.

rows.why: Stock value at cost: 130 units x $5.10 paid per unit = $663.

post.description:
https://proofnotfluff-a11y.github.io/Proofnotfluff-pins/go/free-inventory-turnover-calculator/
Free inventory turnover calculator for online sellers: type units sold per day and units on hand, and it shows days of stock, turns a year and an overstock check.
Extra stock feels safe. In this example, 130 pot holders selling 0.9 a day take 144 days to sell through (130 / 0.9), almost five months. At $5.10 each that is $663 of cash on the shelf. Past the 120-day overstock line, the calculator says stop reordering until it sells down. Example numbers from the free calculator's sample product. A planning estimate, not advice.
